reason: Axes of infructescences have a length, and the examples give lengths.
The hairiness in the examples is probably that of the involucre, phyllaries or stalk, not of the capitulum itself. A rule would need to check which organ the hairs belong to.
A tree crown can be large, and the examples say so.
A corolla or corolla tube can be S-shaped. Some of the examples are about a beak, which is a different part, but the corolla ones are correct.
Ovule orientation (ascending, pendulous) is standard.
Farinose or mealy describes an inflorescence with a powdery surface.
Flattened stalks and blades are meaningful for this anatomy class.
Lobes and similar parts can be broad.
'Structure' is too generic. The examples (connate, dehiscent) are other qualities read as structure. These should map to their own terms.
Scaly surfaces are common on leaves and similar organs.
Petioles can be succulent (fleshy).
The number of drupelets can be few, so this is a count of parts.
'Variable in size' is variation between individuals, not a quality of the fruit. A rule should skip variability words.
Petioles can be keeled or ridged, especially on the abaxial side.
An inflorescence axis has a width, and the examples give widths.
Pollinia and pollen masses can lie horizontally.
'Rays' here are branches of an umbel or inflorescence, not ray flowers. The part is the wrong one.
Decussate describes the arrangement of rays (inflorescence branches), not of ray flowers. The part is the wrong one.
A hypanthium can be small or minute.
The endostome has a length, here compared with the teeth. It is relative, but the quality is length.
A moss costa (midrib) can be strong or weak.
Stems can be nodular or nodulose. One example is about a rhachis, which is a different part.
Ellipsoid grains are prolate spheroids, so a caryopsis can be prolate.
Opercula are often subulate or conic-subulate.
Gemmae have 3-D shapes (spheroid, ovoid, fusiform). The term is generic, so the specific shape term is better when one exists.
Awns can be pigmented.
A moss columella can be exserted beyond the capsule mouth.
Triangular or deltoid shape is meaningful for this part.
A seta can be bent or geniculate.
A rudimentary peristome is standard moss terminology.
Endostome segments can bear cilia. The statement is really about the presence of cilia, but the pair is meaningful.
The neck of a sporangium base can be distinct or indistinct.
The examples are colours (hyaline, yellow, orange-brown), so a colour term fits better than an optical quality. A rule would need to separate hyaline (transparency) from true colours.
The ovate shape belongs to the perforations in the segments, not to the peristome tooth. The bearer is wrong.
The examples say 'rounded', and PATO 'obtuse' is an angle term with a different meaning. The wrong term was picked. A 'rounded' or 'globose' shape term is needed.
A calyptra surface can be rough.
Moss laminal cell walls can be smooth (not papillose).
An embryo can be small.
Radicle position (ventral, dorsal, lateral) is standard for seed descriptions.
This is the number of leaflets (few), which is meaningful.
Legumes can be swollen or inflated.
A receptacle can be narrow.
Bracts can be linear.
Staminate flowers can be borne in fascicles. This is arrangement rather than shape, but the pair is meaningful.
A receptacle can be broad or widened.
A tree crown can be small.
An epicalyx can be flared.
A carpel has a height, and the examples give heights.
Capitula can be borne in fascicles.
Foliage has a colour.
Buttresses can be present or absent on a tree trunk. This is a presence statement.
Bracteoles can be asymmetrical.
Subglobose legumes are spheroid.
The examples are about costal areoles (leaf cell areas in mosses), not the cactus areole bud. The part is the wrong one.
Lobes and tips can be attenuate.
An ovary has a thickness or depth that can be measured.
The number of staminal coronas is an amount.
The examples are widths of the part.
An epichile can be erect.
A leaf sheath can be rolled into a tube. 'Curled' is not exact (the text means rolled), so a 'rolled' term would be better if one exists.
